name: Kyoto
story:
We arrived the week the blossoms turned, which everyone will tell you is luck and nobody will tell you is also chaos. The trick we found by accident: be out by six. Philosopher's Path belongs to joggers and old men with cameras at that hour, and the petals come down the canal like something being delivered.

By nine the city is a different animal. We learned to spend middays in **Nishiki Market** eating things we couldn't name, then retreat north to the quiet temples nobody queues for — Shisen-dō, Manshu-in — where the gardens are raked for an audience of four.

The last night it rained hard. We sat under the eaves of a tiny bar in Pontochō with no English menu and pointed at what the man beside us was drinking. Best decision of the trip.

recs.name: Nishiki Market
recs.note: Go hungry, go early, eat standing up. The tamagoyaki stall at the east end.

recs.name: Philosopher's Path at 6am
recs.note: Two kilometres of canal under cherry trees, entirely empty before seven.

recs.name: Fushimi Inari, after dark
recs.note: The torii gates are lit and almost deserted. Walk up past the first viewpoint — most people turn back there.

recs.name: A machiya in Gion
recs.note: Old wooden townhouse, paper walls, a courtyard the size of a bath mat. Worth the stiff floors.

recs.name: Get an IC card on arrival
recs.note: Buses are the real network here, not the subway, and the card saves endless coin-fumbling.

name: Lisbon
story:
A city that makes you earn every view. We walked roughly twelve kilometres a day, most of it vertical, and ate it all back in custard tarts.

Alfama is the postcard, and it deserves to be, but the evening we remember was in **Graça** — a miradouro, a bottle of vinho verde bought from a kiosk, and a man playing fado to about nine people who all seemed to know him.

recs.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
recs.note: Shellfish by weight, beer by the litre. Expect to queue; it's worth it. Finish with the steak sandwich.

recs.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
recs.note: Highest viewpoint in the city, least crowded. Bring your own bottle.

recs.name: Tram 28, but backwards
recs.note: Ride it from the far end at Martim Moniz to get a seat, or skip it and walk the route.

recs.name: Shoes with grip
recs.note: The pavement is polished limestone. In rain it's an ice rink and that is not a joke.

name: Torres del Paine
story:
Five days on the W trek and four distinct seasons per afternoon. The wind here is not weather, it is a presence — it leans on you, it takes your words sideways, it flattens the lakes into hammered metal.

Day three we got up at three in the morning to climb the moraine to the base of the towers in the dark. Sixty people shivering on rocks in silence, waiting. When the sun hit the granite it went the colour of a struck match and nobody said anything at all for about a minute. Then everyone started crying or laughing. **Worth every step.**

recs.name: Base of the Towers at sunrise
recs.note: Leave Chileno by 3:30am. Head torch, gloves, more layers than feels sane.

recs.name: Refugio Grey
recs.note: Book months out. The deck looks straight onto the glacier and they sell beer.

recs.name: Pack for all four seasons
recs.note: Sun, hail, and 90km/h wind in a single afternoon is a normal day, not a bad one.

name: Marrakech
story:
Sensory overload, in the good way and occasionally in the other way. The medina is a deliberate labyrinth and your phone's map will lie to you with total confidence.

Our best hours were the quiet ones: the **Jardin Majorelle** at opening time, and long afternoons on the riad roof with a pot of tea while the call to prayer went up from four directions at slightly different times.

recs.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa food stalls
recs.note: Pick the busiest one with the most locals. Stall numbers change; crowds don't lie.

recs.name: Any riad inside the medina
recs.note: Courtyard, fountain, roof terrace. The temperature drop walking in from the street is magic.

recs.name: Jardin Majorelle at 8am
recs.note: First slot of the day, before the tour buses. Book online the night before.

recs.name: Carry small notes
recs.note: Nobody has change, ever, and it's always somehow your problem.

name: Reykjavík & the Ring Road
story:
Ten days, one small car, 2,400 kilometres and an almost religious relationship with the weather forecast site. We saw the aurora on night six, from a lay-by somewhere east of Vík, after four nights of cloud and quiet despair.

The real surprise wasn't the famous stuff. It was the **public swimming pools** — every town has one, geothermal, open late, two euros, full of locals discussing the day in water hot enough to hurt.

recs.name: Local pools over the Blue Lagoon
recs.note: Hofsós and Laugardalslaug. A fraction of the price and nobody is filming themselves.

recs.name: Check road.is and vedur.is daily
recs.note: Roads close without much warning. Plans here are suggestions.

recs.name: Drive the Snæfellsnes peninsula
recs.note: Iceland's greatest hits in one day loop, with a tenth of the crowds.

recs.name: Petrol station hot dogs
recs.note: Unironically excellent. Order 'eina með öllu' — one with everything.
